name: bgpstream
desc: For live and historical BGP data analysis
why: Live and historical BGP routing data analysis; a real door into how the internet's routing table behaves.

brief.what_it_is: BGPStream is an open-source software framework for analysing live and historical BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) routing data. You give it a time window, and it finds and fetches the matching archive files from Route Views and RIPE RIS, or reads live updates. The bgpreader command-line tool prints the results to standard output as one line per BGP element (an announcement, withdrawal, RIB entry or state message), or in bgpdump -m format. The homepage also advertises C/C++ and Python APIs (PyBGPStream). The homepage says version V2.2.0 is available now.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes BGPStream as a framework for the analysis of both historical and real-time Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) measurement data. The homepage lists scientific research, operational monitoring, and post-event analysis as its uses.
brief.how_it_works: BGPReader is the command-line front end. By default it uses a 'broker' data interface that finds archive files for the requested time window, so users do not have to download data by hand. Other interfaces read a single MRT file, a CSV list, an SQLite database, or a Kafka topic. Filters on collector, peer ASN, origin ASN, prefix, community and AS-path regex are applied to the stream. Per the docs, the -w option accepts a start and end time, and omitting the end enables live mode.

brief.install_notes: The README says the usual build is ./configure, make, then make install. libcurl must be installed before building the wandio library, and BGPStream also needs wandio (a separate library from WAND at research.wand.net.nz). If you clone from GitHub, run ./autogen.sh before ./configure. Default data access goes to the BGPStream Broker service, so a working internet connection is needed to reach Route Views and RIS archives. I saw no account or API key requirement. The homepage lists Docker and tutorial pages, but I did not fetch them.
brief.standout: Route Views and RIPE RIS archives are presented as one stream you query by time window, and switching from a fixed window to live mode is a single option change. The default output mirrors BGPdump's one-line format, so it can be a drop-in replacement for older scripts.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage advertises V2.2.0 as available now, but I saw no release date or last-commit date on the homepage or README. The GitHub README I read was the classic short build instructions, with no note on whether the project is still developed.
brief.caveats: Building from source needs autotools plus libcurl and wandio, so the build chain is the main obstacle. The README does not state a license; the homepage shows a University of California copyright notice only. Live mode and the Kafka interface are described in the usage text, but I did not test or verify them. The executables list also names parsebgp, which I did not see documented in any page I fetched. Homepage was reachable.

judge.reason: BGPStream turns global routing archives and live updates into a filterable stream, making real Internet route changes inspectable rather than opaque.

entry.title: BGPStream
entry.tldr: Give it a time window and it streams real BGP routing updates from Route Views and RIPE RIS, one line per announcement or withdrawal.
entry.deeper_look:
BGP is the protocol that networks use to tell each other which IP prefixes they can reach. Every route announcement and withdrawal between autonomous systems is part of the record of how the internet's routing shifts over time. Public projects like Route Views and RIPE RIS collect those messages from many vantage points and archive them as MRT files.

BGPStream, from CAIDA, hides the archive hunting. Its command-line tool, `bgpreader`, takes a time window and asks a broker service which archive files cover it. It then prints each BGP element (an announcement, withdrawal, RIB entry or peer state message) as one line on standard output. Filters narrow the stream by collector, peer ASN, origin ASN, prefix, community or AS-path regex. Leave out the end time and it switches to live mode.

The homepage describes the framework as built for scientific research, operational monitoring and post-event analysis. It also advertises C/C++ and Python APIs (PyBGPStream). The command-line tool is the quickest way in: pick a moment when something broke, and read what the routers were saying.

The default output follows BGPdump's one-line format, and `-m` produces the exact `bgpdump -m` format. Per the docs, `bgpreader` can in some cases replace BGPdump in older scripts.
entry.install:
brew install bgpstream
# needs an internet connection: the default data source is the BGPStream Broker service, which points at Route Views and RIPE RIS archives. No account or API key was seen.

entry.whats_unique: Route Views and RIPE RIS archives are exposed as a single stream queried by time window, and moving from history to live monitoring is a one-parameter change.
entry.caveats: The brief found no release date or last-commit date, so how actively it is maintained is unclear. Live mode and the Kafka interface were not tested, and `parsebgp` was not documented on any page read.
